works.name: Marc Bolan Talking to Stevie Dixon, 1973

podcast.title: Glam Predecessor (1969-1970)
podcast.body: Marc Bolan, as the leader of T-Rex, is considered a significant predecessor of glam music. By 1969-1970, he was already exhibiting theatrical behavior in his compositions and videos, defining much of the glam aesthetic, including an androgyne style. "posiblemente el gran predecesor del glam fue el gran disismo Marbola el líder de T-Rex porque ya en 1969 70 tenemos en Marbola incluso composiciones y vídeos de como él ya tenía un comportamiento realmente te atral ya iba definiendo gran parte de la estética del glam y de Zerraval un poco tan escénico con los dupartos con esa estera un poco androjena."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Glam Rock Pioneer (1971)
podcast.body: Marc Bolan, a former rival who became friends with David Bowie, was a key figure in the emergence of glam rock. In March 1971, he appeared on "Top of the Pops" wearing satin clothes and covered with glitter dust, an appearance that profoundly inspired David Bowie. "Bowie had become friends with Mark Bowlin, a former foe he would take an up electric guitars and formed a psych band called T-Rex."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death (September 16, 1977)
podcast.body: Mark Bowen died on September 16, 1977, when his girlfriend, Gloria Jones, crashed their Mini Cooper into a tree in southwest London. "Mark Bowlin died on September 16, 1977, when his girlfriend Gloria Jones drove their mini-cooper into a tree in southwest London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Death in Car Accident (1977)
podcast.body: Mark Bolan, a famous British glam musician and friend of David Bowie, was killed instantly on September 16, 1977, when the Mini he owned, driven by his girlfriend Gloria Jones, crashed. Bolan never learned to drive because he feared dying in a car accident. He had other, larger cars available, including a Rolls-Royce he had lent out to another band that night. "Mark Bowlin was killed instantly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Androgyne Image as Marketing
podcast.body: Marc Bolan's androgyne image was primarily a marketing component, not indicative of true homosexuality. This is contrasted with Joe Brieaz, whose androgyne presentation was described as genuine. "ni Marmola ni de Bid Bowie aunque tenían esa imagen andró general en verdad era mente homosexuales sino que era un muy importante componente de marketing."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Early Career - Taranosaurus Rex
podcast.body: Mark Bowen, a London-based singer-songwriter and poet, began his career with the psychedelic folk band Taranosaurus Rex. This band released four largely acoustic albums in the 1960s but did not achieve significant hit success. "Bowen was a London-based singer-songwriter and poet. He started with a psychedelic folk band called Taranosaurus Rex, who released four largely acoustic albums in the 1960s without managing to have a proper hit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Evolution from Psychedelic Rock/Folk
podcast.body: While Bolan's early work still retained elements of psychedelic rock and folk, it represented a significant evolution towards what would become glam music. This demonstrates his transitional role in the development of the genre. "posiblemente Marbola fue todavía un poco restos de lo que era el róxico del yco pero ya era una enorme evolución hacia lo que sería la música glam."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Glam Rock Appearance on Top of the Pops
podcast.body: In March 1971, after "Ride a White Swan" became a hit, Mark Bowen appeared on Top of the Pops wearing satin clothes and glitter. This striking visual, in a "grey recession-ridden still in the post-war Doldrums England," was seen as fresh and new, further enhanced by Bowen's "petite and cute and non-threatening" appearance which had a "fluid" quality about it. "But in March 1971, Bowen appeared on the show wearing satin clothes and glitter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Guitar Ability
podcast.body: Marc Bolan possessed an "incredible ability to play the guitar," a skill highlighted when comparing him to other artists in the glam movement. "esa increíble habilidad para tocar la guitarra que tenía Marmolan."

srcs.episode: Tras los inicios del Glam. Jobriath

podcast.title: Impact on Sexual Identity
podcast.body: Mark Bowen's glittery, satiny, and somewhat sexually ambiguous public persona on TV, especially given his height of five foot four, resonated deeply in early 1970s Britain, where homosexuality had only recently been decriminalized (1967 Sexual Offences Act) but public displays remained illegal. For some, his appearance pushed boundaries, while for others, it offered a liberating affirmation of their own non-binary feelings. "Now, for some, a pretty glittery, satiny, five foot four Mark Bowen on TV was really close to that line about doing something gay in public. For others, though, it was not just a breath of fresh air. It was also like, hey, that's me. I feel like that. And it's okay to be that way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Tony Visconti's Production
podcast.body: Tony Visconti produced Marc Bolan and "a lot of other great people." "Tony Visconti is, you probably know, David Bowie's producer Mark Bowlin and a lot of other great people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transformation to T-Rex
podcast.body: Frustrated by a lack of success or sensing a shift in the musical landscape, Bowen shortened the band's name to T-Rex and transitioned to playing an electric guitar, which marked a turning point in his career. "Bowen shortened the name to T-Rex and picked up an electric guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Glam Rock Catalyst (1971)
xref.body: In March 1971, T-Rex appeared on the hugely important British TV show "Top of the Pops." During this performance, Marc Bolan, the band's frontman, wore satin clothes and was covered with glitter dust, an event that David Bowie watched at home and found "brilliant," marking it as "the beginning of glam rock" and inspiring Bowie to pursue a similar direction. "In March 1971, T-Rex appeared on top of the pops, the hugely important British TV show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Involved in Marc Bolan's Death (September 16, 1977)
xref.body: Gloria Jones was Mark Bolan's girlfriend and was driving the Mini Cooper when it crashed into a tree in southwest London on September 16, 1977, resulting in Bolan's death. "his girlfriend Gloria Jones drove their mini-cooper into a tree in southwest London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Fan of Marc Bolan and Electric Warrior
xref.body: David Bowie was Mark Bowen's (Bolan's) biggest fan, indicating the strong mutual influence between the two emerging glam artists. "But Bowen's biggest fan was an emerging artist named David Bowie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Friendship with Marc Bolan
xref.body: Bowie and Mark Bowen (Bolan) became close friends, fostering a mutual influence as both artists sensed a shift in the musical landscape. "Bowie and Bowen became close friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

xref.title: Glam Rock Transformation - Haircut and Fashion
xref.body: Inspired by Marc Bolan, Iggy Pop, Lou Reed, and The Legendary Stardust Cowboy, Bowie went "all in" on glam rock. A key element was his haircut, replicated and modified from a model in a magazine wearing Kansai Yamamoto clothes, razor-cut at the sides and back, backcombed into a "puffy fluff ball," and dyed reddish-orange at Yamamoto's suggestion. This, combined with makeup and costuming, transformed him into the "elfin cute boy in the dress" to something "never before seen in music." "Bowie fun to picture of a model in a magazine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
